lessonRef.focus: fair sharing decisions in real situations
lessonRef.title: Transfer, reflection, and publication: fair sharing decisions in real situations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: The example is from a different setting than the problems below.

items.prompt: 29 students need vans that hold 8 students each. How many vans are needed?

steps: The 5 leftover students still need a van.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: 33 students are going on a field trip. Each van holds 4 students. How many vans are needed so every student has a seat?
A baker has 134 eggs and needs 7 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?
A baker has 137 eggs and needs 6 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?
A baker has 70 eggs and needs 3 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: A baker has 58 eggs and needs 4 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A baker has 252 eggs and needs 8 eggs for each cake. How many whole cakes can be made?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
